If we take sound pressure level for both, the difference is the reference pressure used to calculate the level.

Sound pressure level: L = 20 log (p/p0) [dB]

The everyday dB you mention is absolute sound pressure level, calculated with p0 = 20 µPa = 2 × 10^(−5) Pa. The values you give, which top out at 0 dB, are relative levels, calculated with p0 = max(p), that is, the largest value of the sound pressure p, so p/p0 is at most 1. Now look at the curve of the logarithm:

At the maximum of p, p/p0 = 1, and the largest value log(p/p0) can reach is 0. So in the second case, 0 dB is the highest possible level.

The same applies if you replace p with an electrical quantity.
